title: Around is not across
hook: A 3×4 m room. Corner to corner is how far?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Select the correct length formula for boundary versus corner-to-corner routes.

misconception: Every measurement associated with a rectangle is its perimeter.
objective: Select the correct length formula for boundary versus corner-to-corner routes.

claims.text: An ideal rectangle is 4m wide and 3m high. Compare one full perimeter with one diagonal. Scaled model; ideal rectangle; length only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by this lesson's declared expressions; each card prints its working in plain words. At Width=4m, A=14m and B=5m. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2,["+","x",3]]; B=["sqrt",["+",["*","x","x"],9]]; x denotes Width. At x=4, A=14, B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Reset to unverified by demo-builder 2026-10-15 (v2, company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md): v2 stage: plain-words readouts (TP-7a), no 'Full scale' label (TP-7b), money to 2 decimals (TP-7c); A=["*", 2, ["+", "x", 3]], B=["sqrt", ["+", ["*", "x", "x"], 9]], variable {"label": "Width", "start": 4, "min": 1, "max": 8, "unit": "m", "step": 1}. Width 4m, height 3m: along two walls 4+3 = 7m; perimeter 2×(4+3) = 14m; corner to corner sqrt(16+9) = 5m (5×5 = 25 = 4×4 + 3×3). | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): VERIFIED. Own run: at Width 4 m A = 2 × (4 + 3) = 14 m, B = sqrt(16 + 9) = 5 m; readouts '2 × (4 + 3)' and 'corner to corner: 5 × 5 = 4 × 4 + 3 × 3' (no sqrt on screen). Geometry picture: rectangle width x × 10 px, height 30 px (3 m), diagonal drawn corner to corner. Note for demo-builder: at non-integer diagonals the readout prints rounded values with '=' (e.g. Width 1: '3.162 × 3.162 = 1 × 1 + 3 × 3', where 3.162² = 9.998). Record: company/reviews/lh-around-versus-across/2026-10-15-fact-check.md, Pass 51.

claims.text: Perimeter adds all four edges: 2 × (4 + 3) = 14m. Along two walls is 4 + 3 = 7m. Corner to corner is one straight line: 5m, because 5 × 5 = 4 × 4 + 3 × 3. Name the route before you measure.

The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.
